title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things

questions.q: According to Horowitz, why is covering up a crisis a sucker's move?
a: Information always leaks and you under-allocate resources
Employees will quit immediately upon discovering the truth
It prevents the board from taking legal action against you
It makes the company look weak to competitors
questions.why: The crisis lesson lists two reasons: leaks are inevitable and secrecy starves the problem of needed resources.

questions.q: Which type of CEO does Horowitz use Bill Gates as an example of?
a: A One, the strategic visionary
A Two, the practical executor
A hybrid who balances both roles
A founder who never leaves the company
questions.why: The Ones and Twos lesson explicitly names Bill Gates as a good example of a One.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Two from a One in Horowitz's framework?
a: Twos prefer execution and managing over strategic decisions
Twos are always more successful than Ones
Twos focus on fundraising while Ones focus on product
Twos avoid making any decisions at all
questions.why: The Ones and Twos lesson describes Twos as practical CEOs who love to implement and direct teams.

questions.q: What does the text say about the CEO's job being unnatural?
a: You often have to go against what your instincts tell you
You must always follow your gut instinct
You should delegate all uncomfortable decisions
You need to hire a therapist to cope
questions.why: The comfort lesson states the job is unnatural and you will often have to go against your instincts.

questions.q: What company did Ben Horowitz sell to HP for $1.6 billion in 2007?
a: Opsware
Oracle
Salesforce
Intuit
questions.why: The overview states Horowitz sold Opsware to HP for $1.6 billion in cash in 2007.
